findings.title: Regex Injection in Header Filter
findings.description: The `sensitiveHeaders` filter is constructed using `new RegExp`, and while there is an `escapeRegex` function, any misconfiguration or future changes to `sensitiveHeaders` could lead to regex injection.
steps_to_exploit: An attacker influences the contents of `sensitiveHeaders` if exposed through configuration.
The library constructs a regex from user-controlled strings.
The regex logic fails to safely block headers.

findings.title: Regex Injection via sensitiveHeaders
findings.description: The sensitiveHeaders list is converted into a RegExp object using join('|'). While escapeRegex is used, complex or unexpected character inputs could theoretically cause issues in older JS engines.
steps_to_exploit: 1. Supply a malicious header string in options.sensitiveHeaders.
2. Hope that the regex compilation logic fails or behaves unexpectedly to bypass filtering.
findings.impact: Bypassing security filters to leak sensitive headers.
